posts.title: The State of AI, October 2026: Capability Stopped Being the Bottleneck
posts.excerpt: The frontier is a three-lab race decided by 2.7%, benchmarks built for years are saturating in months, and the bottleneck has moved from “can AI do it?” to “can we trust, power and govern it?”
posts.description: A field report on the state of AI as October 2026 ends: the three-lab frontier race, the jagged capability frontier (IMO gold vs 50.1% clock-reading), 88% organizational adoption vs rare profit, the ~$700B compute buildout and its physical limits, and the EU/US regulatory dates that finally landed.

posts.title: Agents in Production: Notes from the 2026 Hype Cycle
posts.excerpt: OSWorld says agents complete two-thirds of computer tasks now — and still fail one in three. What a year of shipping Keja AI, Tapi Learn and AgentReplay taught me about reliability, context and the economics of the agent era.
posts.description: A builder’s field report on production AI agents in 2026: the demo-to-production gap (OSWorld 12% to 66%, still failing one in three), the stack beneath the chat (evals, guardrails, human-in-the-loop as practiced on Keja AI and Tapi Learn), why context is the product, non-developer agent adoption, and the playbook that survived the year.

posts.title: The View from Nairobi: Africa Is Not Waiting for AI
posts.excerpt: Talent pipelines with 63,000+ applications, a national AI strategy with real dates, and products shipping in Swahili and French — the AI story the global discourse keeps missing, from where I sit.
posts.description: The African AI story the global discourse keeps missing: Kenya’s National AI Strategy 2025–2030, the Talent Nation push to train a million African AI engineers, language as a competitive moat (Keja AI in EN·SW·FR), the honest infrastructure constraints, and leapfrog logic from M-Pesa to the agent era.

posts.title: AgentReplay: Deterministic Replay and Counterfactual Debugging for AI Agent Reliability
posts.excerpt: A research-backed whitepaper on AgentReplay — an open-source deterministic replay and counterfactual debugging layer for AI agents. Bit-exact replay with zero model calls. 0.67% overhead, 100% reproduction fidelity.
posts.description: Full whitepaper on AgentReplay — deterministic replay and counterfactual debugging for AI agent reliability. Covers the research foundation (METR time-horizon, ReliabilityBench, the observability gap), the technical architecture (call-site canonicalization, content-addressed blob store, interceptors, replay engine), evaluation results (0.67% overhead vs 5% target, 100% reproduction fidelity), and the 12-week build plan. Open-source at github.com/gadda00/agentreplay.

posts.description: Deep technical breakdown of Busara AI's 50-agent multi-agent DAG pipeline. Covers Kahn's topological sort, parallel execution, circuit breakers, O(1) LRU caching, and 6-stage orchestration in TypeScript.
